newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Guangshen says money used to trade shares.
newsitem.headline: Guangshen says money used to trade shares.

text.p: A Guangshen Railway Co Ltd official on Wednesday confirmed that part of a 300 million yuan investment had been improperly used for share trading.

The China-based firm, which operates a railway between the southern China cities of Guangzhou and Shenzhen, earlier said its chairman and chief accountant had been relieved of their duties after an official investigation into its investments.
The company said the 300 million yuan had been invested in December 1996 with a local finance company for a period of one year without the approval of its board of directors.
But a company official, who requested anonymity, told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin that the investment had been justified.

"We lent the money to it in expectation of returns higher than annual interest rate on one-year bank deposit," the official said. "The financial institution used part of the money to buy (domestic) A shares, which was against our will."
"It's not us but the financial institution which did something wrong," he added.
He said the 300 million yuan did not come from Guangshen's H share issue proceeds of more than four billion yuan raised in 1996, and said there would be no problem in retrieving the funds.

The firm had channelled three billion yuan out of the four billion into projects outlined in the company's H share prospectus and the remaining money is in the pipeline for the projects, the official said.

Guangshen's announcement said it had been notified by its controlling shareholder, Guangzhou Railway (Group) Co, that the parent company would propose the removal of chairman Ge Wenan and accountant Zeng Xianshao from the Guangshen board at a shareholders meeting on June 24.
A proposal will be made to replace them with Li Daihua and Yao Xiaocong respectively, it said.
The firm's H share issue, equity listed by mainland Chinese firms in Hong Kong, has a secondary listing in New York in the form of American Depositary Shares.
